name: Dynamic Graph Benchmark Framework
description: Dynamic graph learning is crucial for modeling real-world systems with evolving relationships and temporal dynamics. However, the lack of a unified benchmark framework in current research has led to inaccurate evaluations of dynamic graph models. This paper highlights the significance of dynamic graph learning and its applications in various domains. It emphasizes the need for a standardized benchmark framework that captures temporal dynamics, evolving graph structures, and downstream task requirements. Establishing a unified benchmark will help researchers understand the strengths and limitations of existing models, foster innovation, and advance dynamic graph learning. In conclusion, this paper identifies the lack of a standardized benchmark framework as a current limitation in dynamic graph learning research . Such a framework will facilitate accurate model evaluation, drive advancements in dynamic graph learning techniques, and enable the development of more effective models for real-world applications.
domain: graph learning / dynamic graph neural networks
evaluation_method: task-dependent (accuracy / AUC / F1 / MRR depending on task)
general_score_metric: task-dependent (commonly AUC or accuracy for classification/link tasks, MRR for ranking/link prediction)
reputation: Recently proposed framework (arXiv 2401.06559); useful conceptual contribution but has limited community adoption so far pending tooling and dataset standardization.
notes: Temporal leakage and evaluation inconsistency across datasets are serious risks; benchmark performance is task- and dataset-dependent; not an LLM benchmark; standardization and dataset curation remain incomplete.
